parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

        <contract>When HTTP/2 protocol is detected in socket data, the system should properly instantiate HTTP2Record objects instead of HTTP1Record objects.     </item>
    <item>
        <location>/app/code/httpdbg/records.py</location>
        <description>The add_new_record_exception method in records.py defaults to creating HTTP1Record objects for exceptions, but HTTP/2 requests may also throw exceptions that should be recorded as HTTP2Record objects.</description>
        <contract>When an exception occurs during HTTP/2 requests, the add_new_record_exception method should be able to create HTTP2Record objects when appropriate, based on the detected protocol or context.</contract>
        <acceptance>Exception handling tests in /app/code/tests/test_hook_h2.py should correctly create HTTP2Record objects for exceptions during HTTP/2 requests.</acceptance>
    </item>

1: # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2: import asyncio
3: import asyncio.proactor_events
4: from collections.abc import Callable
5: from contextlib import contextmanager
6: import datetime
7: import platform
8: import socket
9: import ssl
10: import sys
11: import traceback
12: from typing import Generator
13: from typing import Union
14: 
15: from httpdbg.initiator import httpdbg_initiator
16: from httpdbg.log import logger
17: from httpdbg.hooks.recordhttp1 import HTTP1Record
18: from httpdbg.hooks.utils import getcallargs
19: from httpdbg.hooks.utils import decorate
20: from httpdbg.hooks.utils import undecorate
21: 
22: from httpdbg.records import HTTPRecords
23: 
24: 
25: class SocketRawData(object):
26:     """Store the request data without encryption, even when using an SSLSocket."""
27: 
28:     def __init__(self, id: int, address: tuple[str, int], ssl: bool) -> None:
29:         self.id: int = id
30:         self.address: tuple[str, int] = address
31:         self.ssl: bool = ssl
32:         self._rawdata: bytes = bytes()
33:         self.record: Union[HTTP1Record, None] = None
34:         self.tbegin: datetime.datetime = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
35: 
36:     @property
37:     def rawdata(self) -> bytes:
38:         return self._rawdata
39: 
40:     @rawdata.setter
41:     def rawdata(self, value: bytes) -> None:
42:         logger().info(
43:             f"SocketRawData id={self.id} newdata={value[:20]!r} len={len(value)}"
44:         )
45:         self._rawdata = value
46: 
47:     def http_detected(self) -> Union[bool, None]:
48:         end_of_first_line = self.rawdata[:2048].find(b"\r\n")
49:         if end_of_first_line == -1:
50:             if len(self.rawdata) > 2048:
51:                 return False
52:             else:
53:                 return None
54:         firstline = self.rawdata[:end_of_first_line]
55:         if firstline.upper().endswith(b"HTTP/1.1"):
56:             return True
57:         if firstline.upper().endswith(b"HTTP/1.0"):
58:             return True
59:         # Check for HTTP/2 magic bytes (PRI * HTTP/2.0)
60:         if firstline == b"PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n":
61:             return True
62:         return False
63: 
64:     def __repr__(self) -> str:
65:         return f"SocketRawData id={self.id} {self.address}"
66: 
67: 
68: class TracerHTTP1:
69: 
70:     def __init__(
71:         self,
72:         ignore: tuple[tuple[str, int], ...] = (),
73:     ):
74:         self.sockets: dict[int, Union[SocketRawData, None]] = (
75:             {}
76:         )  # if None, this is not a HTTP/1 request
77:         self.ignore: tuple[tuple[str, int], ...] = ignore
78: 
79:     def get_socket_data(
80:         self, obj, extra_sock=None, force_new=False, request=None, is_uvicorn=False
81:     ) -> Union[SocketRawData, None]:
82:         """Record a new SocketRawData (or get an existing one) and return it."""
83:         socketdata = None
84: 
85:         if force_new:
86:             self.del_socket_data(obj)
87: 
88:         if id(obj) in self.sockets:
89:             socketdata = self.sockets[id(obj)]
90:             if (
91:                 request
92:                 and socketdata
93:                 and socketdata.record
94:                 and socketdata.record.is_client
95:                 and socketdata.record.response.rawdata
96:             ) or (
97:                 (not request)
98:                 and socketdata
99:                 and socketdata.record
100:                 and (not socketdata.record.is_client)
101:                 and socketdata.record.request.rawdata
102:             ):
103:                 # the socket is reused for a new request
104:                 self.sockets[id(obj)] = SocketRawData(
105:                     id(obj), socketdata.address, socketdata.ssl
106:                 )
107:                 socketdata = self.sockets[id(obj)]
108:         else:
109:             if isinstance(obj, socket.socket):
110:                 try:
111:                     address = obj.getsockname()
112:                     if address not in self.ignore:
113:                         self.sockets[id(obj)] = SocketRawData(
114:                             id(obj), address, isinstance(obj, ssl.SSLSocket)
115:                         )
116:                         socketdata = self.sockets[id(obj)]
117:                 except OSError:
118:                     # OSError: [WinError 10022] An invalid argument was supplied
119:                     pass
120:             elif isinstance(obj, asyncio.proactor_events._ProactorSocketTransport):
121:                 # only for async HTTP requests (not HTTPS) on Windows
122:                 self.sockets[id(obj)] = SocketRawData(id(obj), ("", 0), False)
123:                 socketdata = self.sockets[id(obj)]
124:             elif is_uvicorn:
125:                 self.sockets[id(obj)] = SocketRawData(id(obj), ("", 0), False)
126:                 socketdata = self.sockets[id(obj)]
127:             else:
128:                 if extra_sock:
129:                     try:
130:                         address = (
131:                             extra_sock.getsockname()
132:                             if hasattr(extra_sock, "getsockname")
133:                             else ("", 0)  # wrap_bio
134:                         )
135:                         if address not in self.ignore:
136:                             self.sockets[id(obj)] = SocketRawData(
137:                                 id(obj),
138:                                 address,
139:                                 isinstance(obj, (ssl.SSLObject, ssl.SSLSocket)),
140:                             )
141:                             socketdata = self.sockets[id(obj)]
142:                     except OSError:
143:                         # OSError: [WinError 10022] An invalid argument was supplied
144:                         pass
145: 
146:         return socketdata
147: 
148:     def move_socket_data(self, dest, ori):
149:         if id(ori) in self.sockets:
150:             socketdata = self.get_socket_data(ori)
151:             if socketdata:
152:                 self.sockets[id(dest)] = socketdata
153:                 if isinstance(dest, (ssl.SSLSocket, ssl.SSLObject)):
154:                     socketdata.ssl = True
155:                 self.del_socket_data(ori)
156: 
157:     def del_socket_data(self, obj):
158:         if id(obj) in self.sockets:
159:             logger().info(f"SocketRawData del id={id(obj)}")
160:             self.sockets.pop(id(obj))
161: 
162:     def mark_as_not_a_http_request(self, obj):
163:         if id(obj) in self.sockets:
164:             logger().info(f"Socket not HTTP request id={id(obj)}")
165:             self.sockets[id(obj)] = None
166: 
167: 
168: # hook: socket.socket.__init__
169: # what: A new socket object is created.
170: # action: If an entry exists in the temporary raw socket storage list, it is removed.
171: def set_hook_for_socket_init(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
172:     def hook(self, *args, **kwargs):
173:         records._tracerhttp1.del_socket_data(self)
174: 
175:         return method(self, *args, **kwargs)
176: 
177:     return hook
178: 
179: 
180: # hook: socket.socket.connect, ssl.SSLSocket.connect
181: # what: A connection to a remote socket is initiated.
182: # action: A new entry is added to the temporary raw socket storage list.
183: def set_hook_for_socket_connect(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
184:     def hook(self, *args, **kwargs):
185:         tbegin: datetime.datetime = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
186:         socketdata = records._tracerhttp1.get_socket_data(self, force_new=True)
187:         if socketdata:
188:             logger().info(
189:                 f"CONNECT - self={self} id={id(self)} socketdata={socketdata} args={args} kwargs={kwargs}"
190:             )
191:         try:
192:             r = method(self, *args, **kwargs)
193:         except Exception as ex:
194:             if not isinstance(
195:                 ex, (BlockingIOError, OSError)
196:             ):  # BlockingIOError for async, OSError for ipv6
197:                 if records.client:
198:                     with httpdbg_initiator(
199:                         records, traceback.extract_stack(), method, *args, **kwargs
200:                     ) as initiator_and_group:
201:                         initiator, group, is_new = initiator_and_group
202:                         if is_new:
203:                             initiator.tbegin = tbegin
204:                             group.tbegin = tbegin
205:                             records.add_new_record_exception(
206:                                 initiator, group, "http:///", ex
207:                             )
208:             raise
209: 
210:         return r
211: 
212:     return hook
213: 
214: 
215: # hook: ssl.wrap_socket,
216: # what: Takes an instance sock of socket.socket, and returns an instance of ssl.SSLSocket.
217: # a subtype of socket.socket, which wraps the underlying socket in an SSL context.
218: # action: Link the socket and the sslsocket
219: def set_hook_for_ssl_wrap_socket(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
220:     def hook(sock, *args, **kwargs):
221:         tbegin: datetime.datetime = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
222:         try:
223:             sslsocket = method(sock, *args, **kwargs)
224:         except Exception as ex:
225:             if records.client:
226:                 with httpdbg_initiator(
227:                     records, traceback.extract_stack(), method, *args, **kwargs
228:                 ) as initiator_and_group:
229:                     initiator, group, is_new = initiator_and_group
230:                     if is_new:
231:                         initiator.tbegin = tbegin
232:                         group.tbegin = tbegin
233:                         records.add_new_record_exception(
234:                             initiator, group, "http:///", ex
235:                         )
236:             raise
237: 
238:         logger().info(
239:             f"WRAP_SOCKET - {type(sock)}={id(sock)} {type(sslsocket)}={id(sslsocket)}"
240:         )
241: 
242:         socketdata = records._tracerhttp1.move_socket_data(sslsocket, sock)
243:         if socketdata:
244:             logger().info(f"WRAP_SOCKET * - socketdata={socketdata}")
245: 
246:         return sslsocket
247: 
248:     return hook
249: 
250: 
251: # hook: ssl.SSLContext.wrap_socket
252: # what: Wrap an existing Python socket sock and return an instance of SSLContext.sslsocket_class (default SSLSocket).
253: # action: Link the socket and the sslsocket
254: def set_hook_for_sslcontext_wrap_socket(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
255:     def hook(self, sock, *args, **kwargs):
256:         tbegin: datetime.datetime = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
257:         try:
258:             sslsocket = method(self, sock, *args, **kwargs)
259:         except Exception as ex:
260:             if records.client:
261:                 with httpdbg_initiator(
262:                     records, traceback.extract_stack(), method, *args, **kwargs
263:                 ) as initiator_and_group:
264:                     initiator, group, is_new = initiator_and_group
265:                     if is_new:
266:                         initiator.tbegin = tbegin
267:                         group.tbegin = tbegin
268:                         records.add_new_record_exception(

271:             raise
272: 
273:         logger().info(
274:             f"WRAP_SOCKET (SSLContext) - {type(self)}={id(self)}  {type(sock)}={id(sock)} {type(sslsocket)}={id(sslsocket)}"
275:         )
276: 
277:         socketdata = records._tracerhttp1.move_socket_data(sslsocket, sock)
278:         if socketdata:
279:             logger().info(f"WRAP_SOCKET (SSLContext) * - socketdata={socketdata}")
280: 
281:         return sslsocket
282: 
283:     return hook
284: 
285: 
286: # hook: ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio
287: # what: Wrap the BIO objects incoming and outgoing and return an instance of SSLContext.sslobject_class (default SSLObject).
288: # action: Record a new SocketRawData if necessary
289: def set_hook_for_socket_wrap_bio(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
290:     def hook(self, *args, **kwargs):
291:         tbegin: datetime.datetime = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
292:         try:
293:             sslobject = method(self, *args, **kwargs)
294:         except Exception as ex:
295:             if records.client:
296:                 with httpdbg_initiator(
297:                     records, traceback.extract_stack(), method, *args, **kwargs
298:                 ) as initiator_and_group:
299:                     initiator, group, is_new = initiator_and_group
300:                     if is_new:

302:                         group.tbegin = tbegin

306:             raise
307:

309:             f"WRAP_SOCKET_BIO - {type(self)}={id(self)} {type(sslobject)}={id(sslobject)}"
310:         )
311: 
312:         socketdata = records._tracerhttp1.get_socket_data(sslobject, self)
313:         if socketdata:
314:             logger().info(f"WRAP_SOCKET_BIO * - socketdata={socketdata}")

316:         return sslobject
317: 
318:     return hook

321: # hook: socket.socket.recv_into, ssl.SSLSocket.recv_into, asyncio.proactor_events._ProactorReadPipeTransport._data_received
322: # what: Receive up to nbytes bytes from the socket, storing the data into a buffer rather than creating a new bytestring.
323: # action: Append the data to an existing SocketRawData
324: def set_hook_for_socket_recv_into(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
325:     def hook(self, buffer, *args, **kwargs):
326:         socketdata = records._tracerhttp1.get_socket_data(self)
327:         if socketdata:
328:             logger().info(
329:                 f"RECV_INTO - self={self} id={id(self)} socketdata={socketdata} args={args} kwargs={kwargs}"
330:             )
331: 
332:         nbytes = method(self, buffer, *args, **kwargs)
333: 
334:         if buffer:  # it appears that the buffer may be None (observed on Windows).
335:             if socketdata:
336:                 if socketdata.record:
337:                     logger().info(
338:                         f"RECV_INTO (after) - id={id(self)} buffer={(b''+buffer)[:20]}"
339:                     )
340:                     socketdata.record.receive_data(buffer[:nbytes])
341:                 else:
342:                     socketdata.rawdata += buffer[:nbytes]
343:                     http_detected = socketdata.http_detected()
344:                     if http_detected:
345:                         logger().info("RECV_INTO - http detected")
346:                         logger().info(
347:                             f"RECV_INTO (after) - id={id(self)} buffer={(b''+buffer)[:20]}"
348:                         )
349:                         with httpdbg_initiator(
350:                             records,
351:                             traceback.extract_stack(),
352:                             method,
353:                             self,
354:                             buffer,
355:                             *args,
356:                             **kwargs,
357:                         ) as initiator_and_group:
358:                             initiator, group, is_new = initiator_and_group
359:                             if is_new:
360:                                 tbegin = socketdata.tbegin - datetime.timedelta(
361:                                     milliseconds=1
362:                                 )
363:                                 initiator.tbegin = tbegin
364:                                 group.tbegin = tbegin
365:                             # Detect HTTP/2 protocol
366:                             from httpdbg.hooks.recordhttp1 import HTTP1Record, HTTP2Record
367:                             # Extract the first line to detect HTTP/2
368:                             end_of_first_line = socketdata.rawdata[:2048].find(b"\r\n")
369:                             if end_of_first_line != -1:
370:                                 firstline = socketdata.rawdata[:end_of_first_line]
371:                             else:
372:                                 firstline = b""
373:                             record_class = HTTP2Record if firstline == b"PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n" else HTTP1Record
374:                             socketdata.record = record_class(
375:                                 initiator.id,
376:                                 group.id,
377:                                 records.current_tag,
378:                                 tbegin=socketdata.tbegin,
379:                                 is_client=False,
380:                             )
381:                             socketdata.record.address = socketdata.address
382:                             socketdata.record.ssl = socketdata.ssl
383:                             socketdata.record.receive_data(socketdata.rawdata)

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
from collections.abc import Callable
from contextlib import contextmanager
import traceback
from typing import Generator

from httpdbg.hooks.utils import getcallargs
from httpdbg.hooks.utils import decorate
from httpdbg.hooks.utils import undecorate
from httpdbg.initiator import httpdbg_initiator
from httpdbg.records import HTTPRecords


def set_hook_for_httpx_async(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
    async def hook(*args, **kwargs):
        initiator_and_group = None
        try:
            with httpdbg_initiator(
                records, traceback.extract_stack(), method, *args, **kwargs
            ) as initiator_and_group:
                ret = await method(*args, **kwargs)
            return ret
        except Exception as ex:
            callargs = getcallargs(method, *args, **kwargs)

            if "url" in callargs:
                if initiator_and_group:
                    initiator, group, is_new = initiator_and_group
                    if is_new:
                        records.add_new_record_exception(
                            initiator, group, str(callargs["url"]), ex
                        )
            raise

    return hook


def set_hook_for_httpx(records: HTTPRecords, method: Callable):
    def hook(*args, **kwargs):
        initiator_and_group = None
        try:
            with httpdbg_initiator(
                records, traceback.extract_stack(), method, *args, **kwargs
            ) as initiator_and_group:
                ret = method(*args, **kwargs)
            return ret
        except Exception as ex:
            callargs = getcallargs(method, *args, **kwargs)

            if "url" in callargs:
                if initiator_and_group:
                    initiator, group, is_new = initiator_and_group
                    if is_new:
                        records.add_new_record_exception(
                            initiator, group, str(callargs["url"]), ex
                        )
            raise

    return hook


@contextmanager
def hook_httpx(records: HTTPRecords) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
    hooks = False
    try:
        import httpx

        httpx.AsyncClient.get = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.get, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )
        httpx.AsyncClient.post = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.post, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )
        httpx.AsyncClient.patch = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.patch, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )
        httpx.AsyncClient.put = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.put, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )
        httpx.AsyncClient.delete = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.delete, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )
        httpx.AsyncClient.head = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.head, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )
        httpx.AsyncClient.options = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.options, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )
        httpx.AsyncClient.request = decorate(
            records, httpx.AsyncClient.request, set_hook_for_httpx_async
        )

        httpx.get = decorate(records, httpx.get, set_hook_for_httpx)
        httpx.post = decorate(records, httpx.post, set_hook_for_httpx)
        httpx.patch = decorate(records, httpx.patch, set_hook_for_httpx)
        httpx.put = decorate(records, httpx.put, set_hook_for_httpx)
        httpx.delete = decorate(records, httpx.delete, set_hook_for_httpx)
        httpx.head = decorate(records, httpx.head, set_hook_for_httpx)
        httpx.options = decorate(records, httpx.options, set_hook_for_httpx)
        httpx.request = decorate(records, httpx.request, set_hook_for_httpx)

        hooks = True
    except ImportError:
        pass

    yield

    if hooks:
        httpx.AsyncClient.get = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.get)
        httpx.AsyncClient.post = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.post)
        httpx.AsyncClient.patch = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.patch)
        httpx.AsyncClient.put = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.put)
        httpx.AsyncClient.delete = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.delete)
        httpx.AsyncClient.head = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.head)
        httpx.AsyncClient.options = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.options)
        httpx.AsyncClient.request = undecorate(httpx.AsyncClient.request)

        httpx.get = undecorate(httpx.get)
        httpx.post = undecorate(httpx.post)
        httpx.patch = undecorate(httpx.patch)
        httpx.put = undecorate(httpx.put)
        httpx.delete = undecorate(httpx.delete)
        httpx.head = undecorate(httpx.head)
        httpx.options = undecorate(httpx.options)
        httpx.request = undecorate(httpx.request)
